instrument.state: A reproducible failure occurs for a configuration or input composed of multiple removable parts, and candidate reductions can be repeatedly tested.
instrument.operation: Partition the failure-inducing configuration, remove subsets or test their complements, and iteratively retain reductions that continue to reproduce the defined failure.
instrument.signal: Some reduced configurations preserve the failure while others do not, revealing which removals are compatible with continued reproduction.
instrument.inference: The procedure narrows the configuration to a test-relative minimal or near-minimal failure-inducing subset or difference whose retained parts are sufficient to reproduce the observed failure under the test.
instrument.limit: Interactions among parts, nondeterministic failures, unresolved test outcomes, environmental dependence, and the reduction strategy can prevent strong minimization. A retained minimal configuration demonstrates reproducibility under the test, not necessarily the unique underlying causal mechanism.

target.question: Which parts of the proposed onboarding redesign are necessary for users to complete activation, and what interactions prevent a simple feature ranking?
evidence: Synthetic onboarding proposal: six independently switchable interface/rule elements and their dependencies are specified. A resettable replay of a fixed consented usability task supplies a deterministic pass/fail repeatable task test for activation blockage, with unresolved outcomes explicitly possible outside the defined valid configurations. Baseline full configuration reproducibly fails; removing every optional element passes. Deletions preserve a runnable flow only when listed dependency constraints hold.

Every procedure has the same user-error notes, funnel observations, repeatable task test, valid-deletion rules and budget of 80 replay tests. No deletion monotonicity or unique minimal explanation is assumed. Elements can interact; multiple failure-preserving subsets may exist. A fixed identifier order is available for reproducible deletion trials.

Failure means inability to complete this recorded activation task, not real-user population rejection. A failure-preserving subset and the pass results of its valid one-element deletions give bounded evidence about interactions and test-relative necessary elements within that subset, not global feature rankings or universal necessities.

mapping.state: Simplify the failure-inducing input while preserving the oracle’s observed failure. Operational target state: The same reproducibly failing configuration has valid removable elements and the resettable repeatable task test. Decomposition: Replace feature-by-feature priority as the explanatory unit with the retained failure-preserving subset and its tested deletion boundary.
mapping.operation: Run failure-preserving reduction trials: in fixed identifier order try each valid one-element deletion, retain a deletion only when failure recurs, restart from the retained reduced configuration, and stop after a complete pass accepts no deletion or the 80-test budget is exhausted. Next inquiry: The next trial is the next valid deletion from the currently retained failure case; ordinary follow-up examines its observed interaction after the reduction ends.
mapping.signal: Which reduced configurations still fail, which pass and which are unresolved.
mapping.inference: The retained subset reproduces failure. A completed final pass establishes one-deletion minimality among valid deletions under this repeatable task test; a budget stop supports only a reduced sufficient subset. This exposes test-relative interactions, not global necessity or a unique cause.
mapping.limit: Do not assume monotonicity, treat unresolved as failure, or generalize beyond valid deletions and this task; multiple minimal subsets can exist.
